question: Should OpenClaw expose a model-facing `queue_status` queue/workload snapshot, and what visibility, redaction, and permission contract should that tool use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates a public model-facing operational metadata contract affecting privacy, scheduler semantics, and adjacent multi-lane work.

options.title: Approve bounded queue_status
options.body: Add a read-only agent tool backed by a shared snapshot provider, returning redacted lane/capacity/workload data under explicit tool/profile policy.

options.title: Operator diagnostics first
options.body: Settle a permissioned RPC/CLI queue snapshot first, then reuse that backend for a later agent-facing tool.

options.title: Keep visibility operator-only
options.body: Decline model-facing queue visibility and document that dispatcher agents must not rely on internal lane/capacity state.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded queue_status
recommendation.body: Add a read-only agent tool backed by a shared snapshot provider, returning redacted lane/capacity/workload data under explicit tool/profile policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history trail runs through sessions_spawn, command queue snapshots, and agent tool registration, which are central to the API choice.
